points.t: Excessive, symmetrical sweating of the armpits, palms, soles or face that interferes with daily life.
Overactive cholinergic sympathetic signalling to normal eccrine glands (primary), or a systemic cause (secondary).
Exclude secondary causes; aluminium chloride at night; tap-water iontophoresis for hands and feet; specialist botulinum toxin or oral anticholinergics.
Secondary causes: thyrotoxicosis, infection (TB), lymphoma, menopause, drugs (SSRIs), phaeochromocytoma.

items.t: Generalised or night sweats with weight loss, fever or lymph nodes: look for **TB, lymphoma or other systemic disease**.
One-sided or new-onset sweating in later life: consider a neurological cause.

pearls.t: "**New sweating at 40 is secondary until proven otherwise**" — ask about drugs, cocaine, alcohol, sleep, sex and weight.
Aluminium chloride works only on **dry skin at night**, when sweat glands are least active.
Many SSRIs and venlafaxine cause dose-related sweating. Switching or reducing the dose often helps; the evidence for adding an anticholinergic is limited.
